title: DNA
summary: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is the molecule that carries the instructions an organism needs to build and run itself. Explore the double-helix shape, the four base letters that store the code, and how this long molecule is packed inside a cell's nucleus.

plainLanguageExplanation: DNA is the instruction manual of the living cell. It looks like a twisted ladder - a shape called a double helix. The two rails of the ladder are a sugar-and-phosphate backbone, and the rungs are pairs of chemical letters (A pairs with T, and G pairs with C) arranged in a sequence. That sequence is what stores the code, the same way letters of an alphabet store words and sentences. When the cell divides, the DNA is copied so the new cell gets the whole instruction set. Most DNA sits in the nucleus, kept safe, and it directs what the cell builds.

keyFacts.label: Shape
keyFacts.value: A double-stranded, twisted ladder called a double helix

keyFacts.label: Stores
keyFacts.value: The instructions (genetic code) that build and run an organism

keyFacts.label: Base pairs
keyFacts.value: Four bases pair up: A with T, and G with C

keyFacts.label: Where most sits
keyFacts.value: In the nucleus of each cell (and a little in mitochondria)

keyFacts.label: Copying
keyFacts.value: Replication makes an exact copy at cell division

whyItMatters: DNA is why every living thing passes traits from one generation to the next and carries the full plan for building itself. Understanding this molecule unlocks genetics, heredity, and medicine - it's the code behind what makes living things work.
didYouKnow: If you stretched out the DNA in a single human cell, it would be about two meters long - all packed into a nucleus too small to see.
